@@ -0,0 +1,26 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '80'
+title: 'OTel router F: the compaction shortfall log uses the session logger, so TelemetryCapture sees it, and the content-safety test checks it'
+---
+## What
+Found in OTel router task C (01M3MNDXP2G08VKQEZW8MN6F59, ^8mn6f59; see its comments): a compaction shortfall (`Compactor.log`, `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Compaction/Compactor.swift`) logs through a module logger that is made from the global logging system, not through the session's explicit logger. The session pump is a detached task, so a `TelemetryCapture` on the caller's task does not see that record, and `TelemetryContentSafetyTests` does not check it. In production the record still goes to the backend that the executable bootstraps, and it holds only counts.
+
+The router's rule since OTel router A (01M3MND1G818WNMRPDFRAG2E91): a session has an explicit logger (a fork copies it), and no logger is stored in a `static let`. Make the shortfall record use that rule:
+- Give the `Compactor` call the session's logger (or a logger made per call from it), and write the shortfall record through it. Keep the record's message constant and its values as metadata with `RouterTelemetry.LogMetadataKey` keys.
+- Check each other log call that can run on the pump or in a compaction, and make it use the session logger too. Record the list in a task comment.
+- Add the shortfall path to `TelemetryContentSafetyTests`: drive a compaction that has a shortfall, and require the shortfall record in the capture (so the test proves that the record is checked).
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] A compaction shortfall inside a session writes its record through the session's logger, and a `TelemetryCapture` sees it.
+- [ ] `TelemetryContentSafetyTests` requires the shortfall record and checks it for content.
+- [ ] `swift build` passes with no warnings on a clean build.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] A test that drives a compaction shortfall in a session made with the capture's logger, and finds the record.
+- [ ] `swift test` passes one time, and the output shows the full count of tests run.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #otel
\ No newline at end of file

 assignees:
 - claude-code
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m3pgxvanstae41xq214xt706
+  text: |-
+    Research and implementation notes (implement, iteration 1):
+    - Fail-first: I added the shortfall compaction and `expectLogged(containing: Compactor.shortfallLogMessage, metadata: [shortfall: targetLeavesNoRoomForSummary])` to `TelemetryContentSafetyTests` before the fix. `swift test --filter TelemetryContentSafetyTests` ran 1 test in 1 suite and failed with 1 issue: "no log record contains \"a compaction left the live context as it was\"" (TelemetryContentSafetyTests.swift:95). The capture had only the enter records and the rejected-call record. The expectation `shortfall == .targetLeavesNoRoomForSummary(allowedSummaryTokens: 0)` passed, so the shortfall ran and only the record was lost.
+    - How the test makes the shortfall: a second caller compaction with `TokenBudget(limit: tokensAfter, target: 0)`. The target is 0 tokens, so the room for a summary is 0 and no summarizer runs.
+    - Fix: `Compactor.compact` has a new parameter `explicitLogger: Logger? = nil`. It logs the shortfall of the result one time, through `RouterTelemetry.logger(.compaction, explicit:)`. `CompactionCall.shortfallResult` does not log now. The session passes its `explicitLogger`. The message is the constant `Compactor.shortfallLogMessage`; the values are metadata under `LogMetadataKey`. The log call is synchronous; `abandonCompactionIfCancelled` and `runAnswerWork` did not change.
+    - Other log calls that can run on the pump or in a compaction (the check that the task asks for):
+      - Session code (`sessionLogger(_:)`: rejected tool call, generation stall, repetition stop, compaction yield, overflow retry, mail delivery pause, abandoned compaction tier, discovery priming): already use the explicit logger. No change.
+      - `TranscriptEntryMapper` (7 calls: unknown entry kind, prompt schema, unknown segment case, unknown segment carrier, tool-calling mode, encode failure), `PersistableStructuredSegment.generatedContent`, `FileTranscriptRecorder` (append failure, root owner, sync failure), `SessionSidecar` write failure, `SlotPoolLoader.evict`, `RepoMetadata` reader and cache: these are static or shared helpers with no session to ask. The recording path runs on the pump (recordTranscriptDelta, the compaction diff, the run journal). Fix: `RouterTelemetry.pumpJobLogger` (a `TaskLocal<Logger?>`, nil at rest) and `RouterTelemetry.makeLogger(_:)` returns that logger with the category as metadata when it is bound. The pump binds the explicit logger around each job (`withSessionLogger(_:)`, joined with `withSessionMetricsFactory(_:)` in `withSessionTelemetry(_:)`). Thus each of these calls, when it runs in a pump job, goes to the session logger. An actor hop (the recorder actor) keeps the task-local.
+      - `TranscriptReconstruction`, `TranscriptLineDecoding`, `RecordingRootLock`: restore and lock paths on the caller task, not on the pump. A caller-task capture sees them already. No change.
+      - Logs of FoundationModelsExtras on the pump use their own `Logger(label:)`; they are out of the scope of the router.
+    - New test `RouterTelemetryLoggingTests.pumpJobBindsTheExplicitLogger`: a module logger inside `withSessionLogger` on a detached task reaches the capture with the category metadata. The fork test and it share a new `makeSession(in:)` helper.
+    - Filter run: `--filter 'RouterTelemetryLoggingTests|TelemetryContentSafetyTests'` ran 8 tests in 2 suites, all passed; no compiler warning.
+  timestamp: 2026-09-29T12:06:13.589068+00:00
